subject: ventures/tree-service-bid-calculator
auditor: agent session (Claude), independent quality audit, see run record
professional: an owner-estimator of a small residential tree-removal company (ISA Certified Arborist who has bid and run removal crews), who would first check whether the default hours and prices for a typical 24-inch backyard oak and a stump grind land near what the local market pays, and whether the hour factors can be replaced with their own timed crews

evidence.correctness: Ran three scenarios through calc.mjs (scratchpad/tree-service-bid-calculator/run.mjs) and recomputed them in an independent Python script (scratchpad/tree-service-bid-calculator/indep.py) using standard markup-then-margin algebra (price = cost x (1+overhead) / (1-margin)): default two-tree stop 15.1616 on-site h, job cost 5141.75, price 6855.67, $190.44/in (all match); 6-inch 10-ft tree: margin price 298.02, minimum 450 applied (match); 30-inch crane tree near power: 41.67 h, job 15027.57, price 20036.76, proposed $5,000 margin -200.55% (match). Hand-checked the vs-a-flat-per-inch page: pine 0.68 h, cost 397.58, price 530.10, $44.18/in (match). The arithmetic is exactly right. But the outputs a user gets are mis-calibrated against market data the author did not write: the default 24-inch, 60-ft backyard oak prices at $6,529.85 vs HomeAdvisor's $800-$1,500 for a 60-80 ft tree (about 4x even allowing for backyard, structure, stump and haul); the 24-inch stump grind costs 1.8 h x (234+45) = $502 before overhead and margin (~$770 priced) vs $2-$5 per diameter inch ($48-$120) in consumer cost guides; the 30-inch crane removal is 41.7 crew-hours (about five crew days) and $20k. The hour factors are not editable in the page, so the user cannot correct them. Arithmetic right, outputs not trustworthy: 2.
evidence.completeness: README features checked end to end: per-tree hours (pass), stump and haul (pass), travel once and crane once (pass, test 'a crane day is charged once'), loaded labor (pass), overhead then margin price with minimum (pass), per-inch / effective hourly / walk-away / quote floor (present in result), proposed-price check (pass, belowBreakEven flagged), Copy bid summary, Copy bid link and printable proposal (share.mjs, proposal.mjs, tested by share.test.mjs and proposal.test.mjs, 142 tests pass), how-to and two comparison pages present, served page https://marisstella.app/tree-service-bid-calculator/ returns 200. No stubs or TODOs found. Not loaded in a real browser, so UI wiring is credited from page.test.mjs only.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/tree-service-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 142 tests, 142 pass, 0 fail, ~220 ms. Seeded 7 mutations in calc.mjs (each reverted, git status clean afterwards): stump exponent **2 -> **1 (caught, 2 fail), margin divide -> markup multiply (caught, 2 fail), equipment on laborHours instead of onSiteHours (caught, 1 fail), MIN_HEIGHT_FACTOR 0.55 -> 0.5 (caught), haul share on removalHours instead of baseRemovalHours (caught), minimumApplied tolerance 1e-9 -> 1e9 (caught), deadHazard premium 0.2 -> 0.3 (NOT caught: no test sets deadHazard true). Survival 1/7. The comparison page numbers are pinned to calc.mjs by vs-a-flat-per-inch-rate.test.mjs. No test checks any output against an external benchmark.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (237 lines), index.html wiring (lines 311-700), proposal.mjs head and exports, share.mjs exports, calc.test.mjs. calc.mjs is a clean pure module with input validation that throws named errors (e.g. '1,200' DBH throws 'Tree 1: DBH must be a number', shown via clearOutputs(error.message, true) at index.html:584, not a silent fallback). Minor: calc.mjs:11 says 'three lines' while README says four; proposal.mjs is a generated generic copy (platform/proposal/adopt.mjs), deliberate rather than a copied engine; proposed margin returns 0 for a $0 price instead of flagging it.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer and no-warranty text present on README, index and comparison pages; vs-singleops.html avoids invented competitor facts and states non-affiliation (pass). llms.txt source lists github.io URLs but the served llms.txt (curl https://marisstella.app/tree-service-bid-calculator/llms.txt) lists marisstella.app URLs, so no defect there (source-only). Failures: README.md:82 says 'The only thing stored is an anonymous local tally' but the page saves the whole bid (share.mjs saveBid) and the contractor's business block to localStorage, as index.html's own FAQ says; README.md:89 event list omits link_copied, proposal_printed and company_forgotten (index.html:564, 855, 871); the stump-grind claim 'in the range a two-person grind crew actually spends' (index.html:235, calc.mjs:77) is uncited and the hours are then billed at the whole-crew rate plus chipper/truck; the per-inch comparison page's '$3,837.18 below' headline rests entirely on uncalibrated hour factors. Hypotheses in VENTURE.yaml are honestly 'untested'.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an owner enters a backyard oak and a street pine with their wage, burden, dump fee and minimum, and gets a stop price, walk-away and a printable proposal in a minute, with no account. But the number is about four times what the local market quotes for that oak, and the only lever to fix it is the crew wage, because species, access, hazard, haul and stump-grind factors are fixed constants (calc.mjs:19-45, 79) with no input on the page even though the page says 'time your own crews'. A professional would discard the price on the first realistic job.
evidence.domain: Compared against arborist practice and published cost guides. Sound: DBH-squared as a wood-volume stand-in (basal area = 0.005454 x DBH^2 ft^2, so 24 in is 4x 12 in), markup-then-margin algebra, travel and crane charged once per stop, mobilization minimum. Departures: crane access multiplies removal hours by 2.1 and adds a day rate, whereas a crane is used because it cuts climbing and rigging time; stump grinding is billed at the full crew rate plus chipper and truck instead of a grinder operator and grinder rate, and grows with diameter squared while the trade prices stumps per diameter inch; dump fees are per tree rather than per load or ton; near-power work is a +40% premium with no mention that it needs line-clearance-qualified workers (ANSI Z133) or a utility outage; hour constants are uncited.

defects.what: Default hour factors make a typical 24-inch 60-ft backyard oak about $6,530, roughly 4x published market ranges ($800-$1,500 for 60-80 ft trees), and the factors cannot be edited on the page, so a user acting on the default price loses the job or overcharges

Stump grinding is billed at the whole-crew loaded rate plus chipper/truck hourly and grows with diameter squared: a 24-inch stump costs $502 direct (~$770 priced) vs $2-$5 per diameter inch in the trade, while the code comment claims a two-person crew

Crane access multiplies removal hours by 2.1 on top of a crane day rate; a crane is hired because it reduces climbing and rigging hours, so crane jobs are double-charged (30-inch crane tree: 41.7 crew-hours, $20k)
Species, access, hazard, haul and stump-grind factors are hard-coded with no page input, though the page tells the owner to 'time your own crews'
README privacy section says the only thing stored is the usage tally, but the bid and the contractor's business details are also saved to localStorage
README usage events list omits link_copied, proposal_printed and company_forgotten
Uncited claim that grind hours are 'in the range a two-person grind crew actually spends'
deadHazard premium has no test: changing 0.2 to 0.3 leaves all 142 tests green
Dump fee is per tree regardless of size, not per load or ton

verdict: The arithmetic is exact: six outputs recomputed independently (three scenarios plus the comparison page's pine) match calc.mjs to the cent, and the suite (142 tests) caught 6 of 7 seeded mutations. The structure (DBH-squared volume, access and hazards, travel and crane once per stop, markup then margin, minimum) is sound. The numbers it shows are not. With its own defaults it prices a 24-inch backyard oak at about four times published market ranges and a stump grind at five to ten times the per-inch trade rate. It bills grinding at the whole-crew rate, double-charges crane jobs, and gives the owner no way to replace the fixed hour factors with their own timings. The README privacy section is also stale. A tree-service owner would use the layout and throw away the price. It does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2).
